units.title: Helen's Farewell
units.description: El discurso de despedida de Helen: inversión enfática para un registro formal.

content.title: Helen's farewell

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: Twenty years ago, I started this studio at my kitchen table. Little did I know how far it would go.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: Never have I worked with a team as talented, or as stubborn, as this one.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: Not only did you make our clients happy, but you also made me laugh every single day.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: Rarely does a boss get to say that, so I'll say it twice. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: Now, let's address the elephant in the room. Yes, Mark Reed offered to buy us. And no, I didn't accept.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: Only when I saw what Lucía could do did I understand what the future of this studio should look like.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: Losing a few clients to her new studio will be a blessing in disguise. They'll be in excellent hands.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.text: Helen, you're going to make me cry.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: Under no circumstances are you to cry, Lucía. Not tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: And if anyone tells you I'm retiring because I'm tired, take it with a pinch of salt. I'm retiring because I want to sail around Greece.

dialogue.speaker: Helen
dialogue.text: No sooner had I booked the boat than my husband bought a captain's hat. Please, raise your glasses. To Harbour Studio!

content.passage: December. Harbour Studio's farewell party for Helen. The office is full of former clients, colleagues and friends. Helen taps her glass, and the room goes quiet.

content.instructions: Fíjate en el discurso y responde.

content.title: Negative inversion
content.explanation:
Cuando una frase empieza con una expresión negativa o restrictiva, el auxiliar va delante del sujeto, como en una pregunta:
- «Never have I worked with such a team.»

Si no hay auxiliar, se usa «do», «does» o «did»:
- «Rarely does a boss get to say that.»
- «Little did I know…»

Las expresiones más frecuentes son «never», «rarely», «seldom», «little», «not only… but also», «only when» / «only after», «under no circumstances», «no sooner… than», «hardly… when» y «at no time».

Es propia de discursos, escritos formales y de la narración, y da un tono solemne o dramático.

rows: Never
Never have I worked with such a team.
I have never worked with such a team.
Rarely / Seldom
Rarely does a boss get to say that.
A boss rarely gets to say that.
Little
Little did I know how far it would go.
I had no idea how far it would go.
Not only… but also
Not only did you make them happy, but you also made me laugh.
You made them happy and you also made me laugh.
Only when
Only when I saw her work did I understand.
I only understood when I saw her work.
Under no circumstances
Under no circumstances are you to cry.
You must not cry in any situation.
No sooner… than
No sooner had I booked the boat than he bought a hat.
As soon as I booked the boat, he bought a hat.

examples: Never have I worked with a team as talented, or as stubborn, as this one.

Only when I saw what Lucía could do did I understand.
